units.function: agent-based-model-simulates-ten-thousand-agents-from-census-occupational-income-each-agent-attends-college-searches-for-jobs-and-earns-income-government-shields-them-with-welfare-and-a-minimum-wage-three-metrics-income-favors-higher-per-capita-income-and-punishes-a-wage-gap-too-large-or-too-small-education-uses-unemployment-and-the-student-faculty-ratio-equality-compares-the-share-of-women-in-each-occupation-against-earth: We built an agent-based model of ten thousand agents, fed by census data on occupational income. Each agent moves through life by attending college, searching for work and earning income, and the government shields them from harm with welfare and a minimum wage. Three metrics follow. The income metric rewards a higher income per person and punishes a wage gap that is either too wide or too narrow. The education metric reads unemployment as the economic side and the student-to-faculty ratio as the welfare side. The equality metric compares the share of women in each occupation against the same share on Earth
